Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Agribusiness | Economy | National Trade Minister pushes stronger trade and investment ties with Germany Source : Myjoyonline.com 24 November 2026 6:49pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, has called for stronger trade and investment partnerships between Ghana and Germany, with emphasis on industrial development, local production, technology transfer and export growth.
Addressing the sixth German-African Business Summit in Accra, she said the government was committed to translating existing diplomatic relations into meaningful commercial partnerships and investment opportunities.
She noted that trade in goods between Ghana and Germany amounted to approximately €564 million in 2025, describing the figure as an indication of the potential to deepen economic cooperation, particularly in local processing, manufacturing and technical skills development.
Mrs Ofosu-Adjare said Ghana’s position as host of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat offered businesses an opportunity to access markets across the continent.
She, however, stressed the need to strengthen local enterprises to enable them to meet international standards, improve productivity and compete effectively in regional and global markets.
The Minister highlighted government initiatives, including the Feed the Industry Initiative and the Accelerated Export Development Programme, which are aimed at securing raw material supplies, supporting local businesses and expanding Ghana’s export capacity.
She also pointed to Germany’s partnership through the Private Sector and Innovation Promotion in Ghana Programme, which is expected to support more than 1,100 enterprises by 2028.
On efforts to improve the business environment, Mrs Ofosu-Adjare disclosed that her Ministry had developed a proposed Business Regulatory Reform Bill to address overlapping regulations and delays in business approvals.
She said the proposed legislation was intended to simplify regulatory requirements, make compliance easier for businesses and improve the efficiency of their operations.
The Minister urged German and African businesses to use the summit to explore investment opportunities, build stronger commercial relationships and identify practical areas for collaboration.
She expressed confidence that stronger partnerships between Ghanaian and German businesses would accelerate industrial transformation, create employment opportunities, particularly for young people, and support sustainable economic growth.
